newsitem.title: USA: Cooper to sell Kirsch unit to Newell.
newsitem.headline: Cooper to sell Kirsch unit to Newell.

text.p: Cooper Industries Inc said Thursday it had signed a letter of intent to sell its Kirsch division to Newell Co.
Completion of the deal is subject to approval of the boards of both companies, signing of a definitive agreement, and government clearances, Cooper said.
Kirsch, based in Sturgis, Mich., manufactures and distributes drapery hardware and window coverings in the U.S. and abroad.
Cooper said in September it was reviewing strategic alternatives regarding the Kirsch division, including a possible sale.
The division has eight manfacturing and fabrication facilities in North America and five abroad. It has more than 2,400 employees.
Cooper, with 1996 revenues of $5.3 billion, makes electrical products, tools and hardware and automotive products.
Newell, based in Freeport, Ill., makes consumer housewares, hardware and tools, home furnishings and office products. The company posted revenues of $2.9 billion in 1996.
